newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt heats up despite summer doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt heats up despite summer doldrums.

text.p: Debate on cobalt's next price move looked closer to level ground on Tuesday as all sides of the market pondered low nearby stocks in what one trader described as "blistering trading."
"Consumers, producers and traders are waking up to the fact there is no available nearby material on the ground," the trader said.
He expected prices to rise by around three to $4 over the next week, as all concerned eyed the depleted stockpiles.

Others agreed that available material was lacking but did not expect strong gains until the traditionally busy fourth quarter when consumers which have been living hand-to-mouth rush to cover requirements.
"It's still relatively quiet apart from some consumer enquiry who are only probing the market rather than buying large amounts," one London based trader said.
A loss of production at Canada's Falconbridge Ltd Sudbury, Ontario, facility was helping to underpin the bulls' push for higher prices.
One argued that Falconbridge had withdrawn from offering spot material in a market already starved of metal.
The union representing striking workers at Falconbridge said on Monday it was close to reaching an agreement with the mining company on shift scheduling.
Falconbridge's Sudbury production in 1996, including custom feed, was 1,600 tonnes of cobalt, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 45,700 of nickel.

A trader suggested that high grade material could reach between $26 and $30 a pound in the coming weeks. Others in the market said current levels of around $23/$24 were more realistic until consumers return in force.
Elsewhere on the production front traders said that Gecamines of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is said to be running low stock as was its sister African producer Zambia.
